claim.value: Reducing concurrency tests whether contention contributes to export delays, without assuming that contention does contribute.
claim.scope: Rationale for the direction of the proposed perturbation.

provenance.rationale: P010 supplies the hypothesis-testing rationale and explicit non-assumption; P009 identifies the proposed concurrency reduction.

signal_basis.value: Apply and hold a known lower concurrency limit while keeping worker version and other controllable settings fixed. Observe actual concurrency and subsequent queue, completion-rate, and phase-duration responses against baseline and any unchanged comparison pool. Improved object-read or upload durations after actual concurrency falls, relative to comparable baseline and control work, support sensitivity to contention.
signal_basis.scope: A hypothesis test within the tested cohort, concurrency range, versions, and operating conditions. Disturbances and shared-resource contamination can distort the response; no detectable change does not exclude contention.

provenance.rationale: The cited spans supply the controlled perturbation, measured response, comparison, interpretive pattern, and material limits.
This component applies only to CONDITIONAL_WARRANT.

rationale: Lowering concurrent demand provides an informative perturbation of a possible contention mechanism. The resulting temporal and comparative responses can bear on that hypothesis without presupposing its truth. The frozen claim asserts only this testing rationale, not definitive diagnosis or exclusion.
uncertainty: Confounding and limited sensitivity affect how conclusive the test can be, but do not defeat the bounded claim that the reduction tests the contention hypothesis.
